disclaimer: Synthetic example of how to read an influence scorecard from tools an organization already uses. It does not name a target organization, and it is not a map of any real company's stack.
principle: The measurement model does not add a system of record. Each field below is read from a system the organization already has. The names here are one common stack. Swap them for the systems actually in use.
hold_rule: Held means the lesson is verified and the same confirmed mechanism has not come back for the hold window. A recurrence sets the status back to reopened. The repeat stays counted.

fields.link_back: issue link to the lesson issue

root_cause_tag.label: Root-cause tag
root_cause_tag.object: Ticket tag, copied onto the Jira lesson label

owner_team.label: Owner team
owner_team.object: Custom field on the lesson issue

required_links.label: Required links
required_links.object: Issue link on the lesson issue

fields.lesson_to_ticket: Remote link storing the Zendesk ticket id
fields.lesson_to_owner_record: Issue link to the record in the owner team's project
fields.ticket_to_account: Zendesk organization external id matching the Salesforce account id

required_links.rule: Accepted is not counted until the lesson links back to the escalation ticket and to the record in the owner team's own system.

success_plan.label: Success plan
success_plan.object: Task on the account, or a success-plan record

fields.opportunity: Task.WhatId when the renewal is an opportunity
fields.verified_by: Task custom field for the CSM lead or TAM manager
fields.link_back: Task description storing the lesson id

success_plan.note: Customer Success and technical account managers, including strategic TAMs, accept the lesson here. The example system is a CRM. Any CRM that already stores accounts, opportunities, and tasks can hold the same fields.

public_incident.label: Public incident
public_incident.note: Only when the escalation is also a public incident. This practice case is not one.

scorecard.label: Scorecard
scorecard.object: One row per lesson, and one model for the scorecard
scorecard.note: The scorecard is a view over those rows. It is not a new system of record.

owner_teams.name: Support
owner_teams.record: A follow-up ticket the support lead accepts, linked back to the lesson id

owner_teams.name: Customer Success
owner_teams.record: A success-plan task on the account: health or playbook update, outreach to affected customers, and a renewal-risk note. The CSM lead verifies it.

owner_teams.name: Technical Account Managers (including Strategic TAMs)
owner_teams.record: A success-plan task on the account, linked to the opportunity when a renewal is open: customer-specific runbook or architecture review, a check across their accounts, and a QBR follow-up. The TAM manager verifies it. Strategic accounts use the same record.

owner_teams.name: Solutions Architects
owner_teams.record: A lesson issue accepted in the solutions project, linked back to the LESSON issue

owner_teams.name: Data center / hardware operations
owner_teams.record: A lesson issue accepted in the hardware project, linked back to the LESSON issue

owner_teams.name: Product management
owner_teams.record: A lesson issue accepted in the product project, linked back to the LESSON issue

owner_teams.name: Field / professional services engineers
owner_teams.record: A lesson issue accepted in the field project, linked back to the LESSON issue

owner_teams.name: Engineering
owner_teams.record: An ENG issue linked to the LESSON issue
